item: Only 6 independent queries available for the real-LLM evidence base
description: Every cluster-aware CI in this package is necessarily wide; several previously-claimed effects (Borda, is_cyclic) no longer reach significance -- this may reflect genuine absence of effect OR insufficient power to detect a real but small one; this re-analysis cannot distinguish those
priority: high (fundamental data-scarcity limit, not fixable by re-analysis)
recommended_next_step: Would require new real-LLM data collection (more queries) -- explicitly out of scope for this stage (no external API calls permitted)

item: repair_frontier's headroom CI upper bound now exceeds the 0.01 practical-significance threshold
description: Cluster CI [0.0012, 0.0127] no longer sits entirely below 0.01 the way the original row-level CI [0.0029, 0.0084] did -- the 'NO_MEANINGFUL_HEADROOM' decision survives at the point estimate but with less certainty than before
recommended_next_step: Flag explicitly in any manuscript prose that cites this number; do not repeat the original CI without the cluster-aware correction alongside it

item: oracle-style comparisons (repair_frontier's full-frontier oracle) are non-negative by construction
description: The exact sign-flip test is not informative for this specific comparison (all 6 cluster signs are trivially non-negative since the oracle includes the incumbent as a candidate) -- flagged in this package's protocol doc but worth a manuscript-level caveat too
recommended_next_step: Report the cluster bootstrap CI's magnitude, not the sign-flip p-value, when discussing the oracle upper bound

item: extraction_study/repair_diagnostic feature-outcome correlations computed on query-level AGGREGATED features lose within-query variation
description: Aggregating pool_size/provider variation within a query to a single mean (or fraction, for binary features) is the correct query-level approach but discards information about which specific provider/pool-size combination drives an effect -- a legitimate follow-up could model this with a mixed-effects approach instead of simple aggregation
priority: low (current approach is defensible, not wrong)
recommended_next_step: A future stage could fit a mixed-effects model (random intercept per query) as a robustness check, if the 6-query sample is ever expanded
